title: the board-merges refresh test proves no replay by the vessel's own animation, not by how fast CI answers: the 0.15-progress timing bound that flaked twice on 2026-10-05 is replaced by same-animation, same-start-time checks
acceptance: Why. tests/e2e/board-merges.spec.ts:11 ('merge identities queue absent tasks, survive refresh and never replay history') failed only its assertion at :34 `expect(afterRefresh-beforeRefresh).toBeLessThan(.15)` on two PRs that cannot affect the board: run 37218356637 on #179 (T-190, autopilot Python only) measured 0.185, run 37218411231 on #180 measured 0.176. Both were rerun as flakes with a PR comment. main's runs at 4230965, 4028a86 and 84ed638 passed it.

Diagnosis. The measured value is the change in `getComputedTiming().progress` of the vessel's `heel` CSS animation (board/public/ship.css:177, 1.8 s) between two separate `evaluate` calls (:23-26 and :29-32). Between them the test performs a `fetch('/api/state')` plus `render` in a third `evaluate` (:27) and a Playwright `expect(...).toHaveAttribute` poll (:28), each a browser round trip. Progress is linear in wall time for an animation that is not restarted, so the value is simply (elapsed wall time between the two samples) / 1.8 s; 0.15 is 270 ms. Under CI load those round trips exceed 270 ms with no defect in the board. The bound measures CI latency, not replay.

The property this test protects is unchanged: a redraw (`render`) while a merge effect is in progress keeps the same running animation, neither restarting it (board/public/ship.js:279-287 keeps transient classes and their `animationDelay` across `sync`) nor seeking it, and `applyEffect` (ship.js:772-797) does not re-add `heel` with a new delay. tests/e2e/game.spec.ts:126-139 already measures this kind of property in one browser turn ('so elapsed browser transport time cannot masquerade as an animation reset'); follow that precedent.

Change, in tests/e2e/board-merges.spec.ts only, replacing :23-34 (keep the `waitForTimeout(700)` at :22 so the sample is mid-effect, and keep :35 onward unchanged):
- One `page.evaluate` that first fetches `/api/state` and awaits its JSON, then, with no further await before `render`: takes `const el = document.querySelector('#vessel')`, `const a0 = el.getAnimations()[0]`, records `a0`'s existence, `playState`, `startTime`, `animationName` and `a0.effect.getTiming().delay`, calls `window.render(state)` synchronously, then takes `a1 = el.getAnimations()[0]` and `el === document.querySelector('#vessel')`.
- It returns plain values: `hasAnimation` (a0 exists), `running` (a0.playState === 'running'), `name` (a0.animationName), `sameVessel`, `sameAnimation` (a1 === a0), `startBefore` and `startAfter` (a0.startTime before render and a1.startTime after), and `delayBefore` and `delayAfter` (`effect.getTiming().delay` of a0 before render and of a1 after).
- The test asserts `hasAnimation` true, `running` true, `name` 'heel', `sameVessel` true, `sameAnimation` true `startAfter` equal to `startBefore`, and `delayAfter` equal to `delayBefore`. A restart (a new CSSAnimation) fails `sameAnimation`; a seek or a restart of the same animation changes `startTime`; a re-applied negative `animation-delay` keeps the CSSAnimation and its `startTime` but changes its effect's `delay`, which the delay equality catches. None of these depend on how long CI takes.
- The existing `expect(page.locator('.scene')).toHaveAttribute('data-effect','merge:881')` after the redraw (:28) and the `animationDelay` '0s' check (:35) stay.
- No numeric progress or wall-time bound remains in this test.

Fail-first. The new assertions must fail against a board that restarts or shifts the animation on redraw. The worker shows this by reasoning in the PR body, not by running suites, using mutations that really do so in Chromium: (a) if `sync` replaced the `#vessel` node instead of keeping it (ship.js:276-277 taking the `cloneNode` branch), `sameVessel` and `sameAnimation` fail; (b) if `applyEffect` removed `heel`, forced a style flush (e.g. `void target.offsetWidth`) and re-added it, a new CSSAnimation starts and `sameAnimation` fails; (c) if `applyEffect` re-applied `target.style.animationDelay = `${-elapsed}s`` on every redraw (dropping the `classList.contains` guard at ship.js:789), the effect's `delay` changes and `delayAfter` differs. Note that removing and re-adding the class in one synchronous turn without a flush does not restart a CSS animation, so that is not a valid fail-first example. Workers do not run the suites; the required GitHub check and the gates verify.

Out of scope: board/public/**, the other tests in board-merges.spec.ts (including :37-40, whose 4 s window is a 'not replayed' bound already justified in its comment and not part of this flake), game.spec.ts, and design.md (no design text describes this assertion; design.md:2059 describes the merge effect, which does not change).
No rule changes and no work in flight is affected: this edits one test's assertions.
